body:
Provide a reusable manifest entrypoint for validation of official Repo2RLEnv exports, preserving original task/grading assets without per-task human/LLM repairs. Subissue of #33.

**Status:** [PR #46](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/pull/46) is open and unmerged. The CLI covers planning, fixed-job recovery, CPU admission, native control classification, verified local/HF preservation and exact-worker cleanup. Forty-one offline tests and GitHub’s Code quality/Tests checks pass. [Results and limitations](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/42be192b/experiments/44-validation-entrypoint/results.md).

**Native evidence:** unchanged Cobrapy #1482 reproduced nop 0/oracle 1 with a clean oracle command; Scanpy #4389 reproduced its apt prerequisite failure before controls. The final controller repeated the positive clean Cobrapy result. All three workflows verified anonymous HF readback and empty owned-resource cleanup; completed reinvocations were inert. All ten files/modes per reference remained unchanged. No task or environment repair was added.

**Supported scope:** pinned native-inline Repo2RLEnv `27d04ee8`, Harbor 0.6.6, original grading/timeouts, serial validation on existing reserved Iris CPUs with a POSIX controller/Linux x86-64 workers. Recorded initializers and generation remain separate; #45 investigates the official generation/export handoff. Cohort portability, grader robustness and task-release readiness remain unproven.

**Budget/review:** #44 used 0.399823 additional allocated CPU-hours; epic total 6.764819/32, no outstanding CPU reservations, new model calls or new capacity. Existing $10 archival reservation remains unreconciled within the $90 operating ceiling, strictly below the user’s $100 extra limit. Native evidence and logs are linked in comments. Keep this issue and #33 open for review; no automatic merge.

🤖 Started from reverified main `2a1950d239f1ada467c35393991dac87debe35f7` on fresh branch `codex/pipeline/manifest-validation`. Research branches remain separate and unmerged. Initial inspection confirms the installed CLI currently only lists/reads prompts; the repeatedly exercised fixed-handle journal and manifest adapters are the starting point for extraction.

The supported interface still needs implementation, meaningful failure/recovery tests and documentation. Initialization, execution transport, original grading/completeness and publication eligibility must remain distinct contracts; #39’s OHIF-specific probes/strict gates cannot silently become universal policy. Official pipeline/native baseline settings stay explicit. No PR or production entrypoint is claimed yet; no new native reservation/model call/new capacity. Current epic actual is 6.364996 CPUh, zero CPU reservations, existing archival reservation unreconciled. [Authoritative next step](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/64ea12e0/experiments/33-unattended-validation/next-step.json).

🤖 [Implementation cb3d2b78](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/commit/cb3d2b78) and [pre-admission evidence 803a6b00](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/803a6b00/experiments/44-validation-entrypoint/pre-admission-checkpoint.json) are published. All 34 offline tests pass, including installed worker resources, seven durable effect boundaries, uncertain/missing submission recovery, early empty output, negative classification, partial public upload, budget and retention gates. These fixtures are not native scientific evidence.

The installed CLI accepted both unchanged #38 reference exports. Cobrapy #1482 is now running as `/exedev/biotasks-val-issue44-native-80e39b1688d7` on existing reserved TRC worker 0055 (`c7c14a252d`), with 6⅓ CPU-hours reserved for its main/stop/cleanup jobs. Scanpy #4389 is not admitted until this workflow resolves. Expected comparisons are the former positive clean Cobrapy pair and Scanpy’s prerequisite failure; no task/bootstrap repair, timeout increase, models or new capacity. Original verifier deadlines and eight grading assets per export remain unchanged. Outer reservation now accounts for both builds plus full control windows.

Infrastructure preservation change: stop execution, seal/copy evidence, retain the volume until verified durable readback, then perform exact-worker cleanup. An attempted empty output becomes a stop-only salvage hold. Source notices were restored by anonymous hash-verified reads from #38’s eligible snapshots. Public archival remains under the existing epic reservation and excludes images, environments, wheels, biological datasets and Matchms. Native outcomes/archival/cleanup are pending; no PR or production-readiness claim yet.

🤖 The unchanged Cobrapy #1482 reference reproduced its native positive/clean outcome: nop reward 0, oracle reward 1, both original tracked F2P tests passing under the oracle and all 17 P2P tests passing on both sides. Both native wrapper commands exited 0; oracle whole test command exited 0. The classifier verified original task/mode hashes, source/image identity, native wheel source parity and original grading assets before assigning these flags. This is validation of an existing export, not a newly generated task or a broader quality claim.

Primary allocation was 0.176825556 CPU-hours. Its eligible evidence passed anonymous HF readback at [snapshot c2fd5966](https://huggingface.co/buckets/open-athena/biotasks/tree/research/44-validation-entrypoint/2026-10-24/c2fd59661042aafe4eb3647c30802595cb17065884a088b81abd6b9f78f1c975). Exact-worker cleanup is pending; the volume remains retained until that proof. Scanpy is still unadmitted. Models and new capacity remain disabled.

🤖 The supported validation component is ready for review in [PR #46](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/pull/46), open/unmerged. All **41 offline tests** and both GitHub checks pass. This includes real installed-wheel resources/SDK isolation and budget-overrun recovery that closes new admission while allowing already reserved preservation/cleanup to finish.

Native comparison: unchanged Cobrapy #1482 reproduced nop 0/oracle 1, oracle 2/2 F2P and 17/17 P2P, clean whole-command exit 0; Scanpy #4389 reproduced apt exit 100 before controls (`cmake`/Python 3.13 packages unavailable). The final controller repeated the clean positive Cobrapy case. All ten files/modes per reference matched the frozen source; no task, timeout or bootstrap repair was added. [Detailed comparison and six native primary/cleanup snapshots](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/42be192b/experiments/44-validation-entrypoint/results.md).

Every workflow verified anonymous HF readback before exact-worker cleanup, and every owned-resource inventory was empty with the shared public base preserved. Completed native reinvocations forbade transport and left 261 baseline / 143 final-run files and the budget unchanged. Native grading/worker/recipe/classifier/journal code was unchanged by subsequent host-only budget and SDK-isolation corrections; their negative regressions failed before the fixes and pass afterward.

The final metadata/source/check bundle has 124 members, 71,161 compressed bytes and two anonymously verified objects: [snapshot 13011529](https://huggingface.co/buckets/open-athena/biotasks/tree/research/44-validation-entrypoint/2026-10-24/13011529b85552c1a941da15c5c6e7105bd9fa2dc96affd2664569431033cf85), [Git-versioned manifest](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/323a770f/experiments/44-validation-entrypoint/final-evidence-manifest.json). Disposable local check/staging copies were removed after verified preservation. Canonical evidence and exact-version resumption inputs remain under HOME for review; no task data depends on `/tmp`.

#44 used **0.399822778 allocated CPU-hours**; epic total **6.764818889/32**, reservations 0, new model calls 0/new capacity false. The existing $10 archival reservation remains unreconciled within the $90 operating ceiling. Historical 83 exports/82 ever-positive/67 ever-clean are unchanged; these are repeated controls, not new task generation. The full generation/validation goal remains active under #45’s official handoff question. Keep #44/#33 open for review; no automatic merge.
